auth.description: Airtable access token sent as a bearer — a personal access token or an OAuth-issued one
auth.name: airtable.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

description: Airtable records: read, create, update and delete a record in a base's table

contract.description: Read one record from a table — its cell values are under `fields` in the response, keyed by column name. Returns every column the token can see, in Airtable's default JSON cell format: narrowing or reformatting them needs the `fields[]` and `cellFormat` query parameters this connector cannot encode. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/error/message`, its error code at `/error/type` in the response body.

operations.description: Read one record from a table — its cell values are under `fields` in the response, keyed by column name. Returns every column the token can see, in Airtable's default JSON cell format: narrowing or reformatting them needs the `fields[]` and `cellFormat` query parameters this connector cannot encode

params.description: The base's id, the `app…` segment in the base's URL in Airtable
params.name: base_id

params.description: The table's id, the `tbl…` segment in the table's URL in Airtable. Airtable also routes this segment on a table *name*, which this connector does not accept: a name is interpolated into the URL unencoded, so one containing a space or a `/` would address the wrong route
params.name: table_id

params.description: The record's id, `rec…`. It is what a create returns and what the record's own URL ends with
params.name: record_id

fields.description: The record's cell values, keyed by column name. Individual columns are not enumerated: they are the base's own schema, which differs per base and changes at runtime — recording the envelope is what a consumer cannot infer

contract.description: Create one record in a table. Cell values are supplied under `fields`, keyed by column name, and must already be in the exact JSON form each column expects — Airtable's `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet (see the connector's notes). The created record, with its `rec…` id, is in the response. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/error/message`, its error code at `/error/type` in the response body.

operations.description: Create one record in a table. Cell values are supplied under `fields`, keyed by column name, and must already be in the exact JSON form each column expects — Airtable's `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet (see the connector's notes). The created record, with its `rec…` id, is in the response

params.description: The base's id, the `app…` segment in the base's URL in Airtable
params.name: base_id

params.description: The table's id, the `tbl…` segment in the table's URL in Airtable. The name form is not accepted — see `airtable-record-get`
params.name: table_id

params.description: The record's cell values, as an object keyed by the table's column names — `{"Name": "Acme", "Status": "Open"}`. Each value must match its column's type: a single-select takes one of its configured option names, a linked-record column takes an array of `rec…` ids, a date takes an ISO 8601 string. An unknown column name is rejected, not ignored
params.name: cell_values

schema.description: A map from column name to cell value. Untyped here because the columns are the base's own schema

fields.description: The created record's cell values as Airtable stored them, keyed by column name. Computed and formula columns appear here having been evaluated

id.description: The created record's id — what later calls address it by

contract.description: Update one record's cell values. The write is sparse: only the columns named in `fields` change and every other column of the record is left exactly as it was. Values must already be in the form each column expects — `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet. The updated record is in the response. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/error/message`, its error code at `/error/type` in the response body.

operations.description: Update one record's cell values. The write is sparse: only the columns named in `fields` change and every other column of the record is left exactly as it was. Values must already be in the form each column expects — `typecast` coercion cannot be requested yet. The updated record is in the response

params.description: The base's id, the `app…` segment in the base's URL in Airtable
params.name: base_id

params.description: The table's id, the `tbl…` segment in the table's URL in Airtable. The name form is not accepted — see `airtable-record-get`
params.name: table_id

params.description: The id of the record to update
params.name: record_id

params.description: The columns to change, as an object keyed by the table's column names. Columns not named here keep their current values. Setting a column to `null` clears it, which is the only way to empty a cell through this operation
params.name: cell_values

schema.description: A map from column name to cell value. Untyped here because the columns are the base's own schema

createdTime.description: When the record was created — unchanged by an update

fields.description: The record's cell values after the update, keyed by column name. Every column is returned, not only the changed ones

contract.description: Delete one record and every cell value in it. There is no API route back: Airtable's trash and revision history are UI features on a retention window, not endpoints, so a flux run cannot undo this. Responds `{"id": …, "deleted": true}`. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/error/message`, its error code at `/error/type` in the response body.

operations.description: Delete one record and every cell value in it. There is no API route back: Airtable's trash and revision history are UI features on a retention window, not endpoints, so a flux run cannot undo this. Responds `{"id": …, "deleted": true}`

params.description: The base's id, the `app…` segment in the base's URL in Airtable
params.name: base_id

params.description: The table's id, the `tbl…` segment in the table's URL in Airtable. The name form is not accepted — see `airtable-record-get`
params.name: table_id

params.description: The id of the record to delete
params.name: record_id

deleted.description: Always `true` on a 2xx. Airtable reports a record that was already gone as a 404 rather than as `false`

id.description: The id of the record that was deleted
